1.explanation: The file report-renderer.js is responsible for grouping audits into passing and failing sets and for inserting the “View N passed items” details summary into the DOM. It always generates that section regardless of N. The details-renderer.js module builds the <details> and <summary> elements around each group’s items. To fix the bug, report-renderer.js needs to skip rendering the passed-items <details> entirely when the count is 0, and/or details-renderer.js needs to omit the <summary> when there are no child audits. These are the two modules where the passed-audit dropdown is created and should be adjusted to gate against a zero count.
1.bug_scenario: In the Lighthouse report UI v2, when there are zero passing audits the “View 0 passed items” dropdown control is still rendered—even though there’s nothing inside to show. The screenshot shows the passed-items details summary with an arrow, but clicking it reveals no content. The desired behavior is to suppress the entire details dropdown when the passed count is zero.

2.explanation: All of the v2 report UI logic lives under lighthouse-core/report/v2/renderer. details-renderer.js is where the code unconditionally builds the "passed audits" section (and its "View X passed items" toggle), report-renderer.js orchestrates grouping and always passes through an empty passed list into details-renderer, and dom.js provides the DOM construction utilities that actually create the <details> element and summary text. To prevent the zero-count dropdown from appearing, you need to modify details-renderer.js (and its caller in report-renderer.js) to skip rendering the passed-items <details> entirely when the passed-items array is empty.
2.bug_scenario: In the Lighthouse v2 report UI, when no audits have passed ("0 passing audits"), the report still renders a collapsed “View 0 passed items” dropdown toggle at the bottom. Since there are no passed audits to show, the dropdown is misleading and should be omitted entirely.
